caption: TP3 (Appendix A), ground truth: the LL optimal value function $f^*(\mathbf{x})=f(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}^*(\mathbf{x}))$ on a 61 x 61 grid over the UL box [0, 15]^2. The LL problem min ||x - y||^2 over y in [0, 10]^2 is a strictly convex quadratic programme, so y*(x) = min(x, 10) is single-valued, as Assumption A2 requires; it was solved by bounded-variable least squares (SciPy lsq_linear, 'bvls') and checked against the closed-form projection. The kinks at x_i = 10 are where the LL bound becomes active. The open circle marks the bilevel optimum x* = (15, 10), y* = (10, 10), theta = 325, f* = 25; the blue lines on the floor are the UL constraint boundaries x1 + 2 x2 = 30 (solid) and x1 + x2 = 25 (dashed). Ground truth only; no method was charged.

TP3 (Appendix A), ground truth: the UL objective on the follower's response, $\theta(\mathbf{x})=F(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}^*(\mathbf{x}))$ on a 61 x 61 grid over the UL box [0, 15]^2. The LL problem min ||x - y||^2 over y in [0, 10]^2 is a strictly convex quadratic programme, so y*(x) = min(x, 10) is single-valued, as Assumption A2 requires; it was solved by bounded-variable least squares (SciPy lsq_linear, 'bvls') and checked against the closed-form projection. The kinks at x_i = 10 are where the LL bound becomes active. The open circle marks the bilevel optimum x* = (15, 10), y* = (10, 10), theta = 325, f* = 25; the blue lines on the floor are the UL constraint boundaries x1 + 2 x2 = 30 (solid) and x1 + x2 = 25 (dashed). Ground truth only; no method was charged.

TP3, SA-APPA (M1), run 5 (seed 5), selected by a rule fixed in advance: the lower median (15th of 30) of the locked final UL objectives. The GP is the one SA-APPA held after the 25-point initial design, trained on 25 truly evaluated points with its own settings (squared-exponential kernel, lengthscale 8.01 from the median heuristic, signal variance 1, outputs mean-centred and not rescaled); no hyperparameter was tuned for this figure. Grey: true theta(x); blue: GP posterior mean; black: training points; open circle: optimum x* = (15, 10), theta = 325; cross: SA-APPA's best feasible evaluated point at this stage, x = (14.58, 8.40), theta = 340.48. On 2,500 held-out points over the box the mean has RMSE 10.66 and maximum absolute error 69.6 (theta spans 1032); within 1.5 of x* the RMSE is 2.60.

TP3, SA-APPA (M1), run 5 (seed 5), selected by a rule fixed in advance: the lower median (15th of 30) of the locked final UL objectives. The GP is the one SA-APPA held after the 25-point initial design, trained on 25 truly evaluated points with its own settings (squared-exponential kernel, lengthscale 8.01 from the median heuristic, signal variance 1, outputs mean-centred and not rescaled); no hyperparameter was tuned for this figure. Uncertainty of the GP: the surfaces mu +/- 2 sigma (multiplier 2) and the true theta. Because the signal variance is fixed at 1 while theta varies by about 1032, sigma is at most 1 and averages 0.0046; the two surfaces are indistinguishable at this scale. The empirical coverage of the +/- 2 sigma interval on 2,500 held-out points is 0.0% over the box and 0.2% within 1.5 of x*, against a nominal 95%: the GP's predictive uncertainty is not calibrated on this problem.

TP3, SA-APPA (M1), run 5 (seed 5), selected by a rule fixed in advance: the lower median (15th of 30) of the locked final UL objectives. The GP is the one SA-APPA held after the 25-point initial design, trained on 25 truly evaluated points with its own settings (squared-exponential kernel, lengthscale 8.01 from the median heuristic, signal variance 1, outputs mean-centred and not rescaled); no hyperparameter was tuned for this figure. Absolute error of the GP mean on a 61 x 61 grid, with training points (dots), the optimum (open circle), the UL constraint boundaries (black) and the LL kink lines x_i = 10 (dotted). The error is largest at (14.5, 15.0), away from the training points; inside the feasible region it is smaller but does not vanish near the kink x_2 = 10, on which the optimum lies, because the smooth kernel cannot represent the change of slope there.

SMD6 at (3, 3): the 60 UL values that SA-APPA trained its GP on (run 1, the lower-median run) against the optimistic theta at the same points. The LL of SMD6 is optimal on a whole line of tail variables (t1 = t2), and the UL objective adds the squared tail, so the nested differential-evolution solve returns theta_opt + 2 t^2 with t effectively arbitrary. The gap is non-negative everywhere, with median 32.7 and maximum 180.7; the dashed line is equality.

SMD6 at (3, 3), 200 held-out points: GP mean against the optimistic theta. Grey squares: the GP SA-APPA held at the end of run 1 (RMSE 204, correlation 0.18). Blue circles: a diagnostic GP with the same kernel, hyperparameter rule and 60 training inputs, but trained on the optimistic theta at those inputs (RMSE 10.0, correlation 0.98). The diagnostic GP is not an SA-APPA run; it shows that the poor fit comes from the inconsistent LL responses rather than from the GP model.

Budget composition, TP1-TP9, internal ablation, design and engine (M1-M6).
